title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 316–317 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck studies the outer action of Γ on π̂_{0,3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, which is free profinite on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. Here Γ is Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q), but he also treats it as an abstract group of automorphisms whose elements must satisfy conditions. The arithmetic fundamental group E_{0,3} is an extension 1 → π̂_{0,3} → E_{0,3} → Γ → 1.

This page writes diagram (σ), a morphism of extensions of Γ. The left vertical map φ̂ : π̂_{0,3} → Ĝ^+_{0,3} is surjective. Its target is the quotient of π̂_{0,3} by the closed normal subgroup generated by l_1^2 and l_∞^3. This quotient is the 'fundamental group with singularities' (the orbifold or stack fundamental group) of the orbifold (P^1_Q − {0}, 2·{1} + 3·{∞}). It is the profinite completion of Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL_2(Z), i.e. the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line. Here 0 plays the role of the cusp, 1 the elliptic point of order 2 and ∞ that of order 3. The loop l_0 = (l_1 l_∞)^{-1} keeps infinite order and is the parabolic element. M_{0,3} is the corresponding extension of Γ by this group. Φ lifts φ̂ Γ-equivariantly.

On the previous page he says a homomorphism (3) commuting with the Γ-action is an a priori non-trivial condition on each element of Γ. He wants it made explicit in terms of the computations in [C], alongside the congruence conditions. Here he restates the condition as the existence of the morphism of extensions (σ).

The quotient by l_1^2 and l_∞^3 makes the relevant symmetries visible. The order-2 and order-3 elliptic points of the j-line are the images of the S_3-symmetries of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, whose quotient by S_3 is the j-line orbifold. Compatibility of the Γ-action with these 2- and 3-torsion phenomena is what the next page turns into explicit equations. There he takes outer actions commuting with S_3, normalised to commute with σ_∞, parametrised by pairs (g_0, ρ) with ρ ∈ Ẑ*. He imposes relations (9), (10) and (10bis), the last being a product of three ρ-conjugates equal to 1. The margin notes γ = (ρ−1)/2. These are Drinfeld's 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations for GT, with m = (λ−1)/2.

The page ends with the programmatic remark that he suspects 'toute une kyrielle de conditions de même nature sur Γ' which one should extract more generally. That is, the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in Out(π̂_{0,3}) should be cut out by a whole family of such geometric compatibility conditions coming from orbifold quotients. This is the germ of the Esquisse's Teichmüller-tower description of Γ_Q and of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One subtlety is left unstated. If an element of Γ sends each l_x to a conjugate of l_x^λ (the inertia/cyclotomic condition), the normal closure of l_1^2 and l_∞^3 is automatically preserved, so some descended action on the quotient always exists. The genuinely non-trivial content must therefore be compatibility with a pre-given extension M_{0,3} or homomorphism (3), presumably coming from the S_3-quotient description in [C]. The page does not spell out which; the reader must take it from the previous page.

The notation for the quotient group is inconsistent: Ĝ^+_{0,3} on this page versus what the previous-page transcription reads as \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}. It is presumably one and the same group, the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) or a '+' variant of it.

ideas.what: The profinite orbifold fundamental group of P^1 − {0} with weights 2 at 1 and 3 at ∞, presented as π̂_{0,3}/⟨⟨l_1^2, l_∞^3⟩⟩. It is (Z/2 * Z/3)^ = PSL_2(Z)^, the j-line orbifold, and carries an arithmetic Γ_Q-extension M_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Étale fundamental group of a root stack / stacky curve; profinite PSL_2(Z) as π_1 of the moduli stack M_{1,1} (coarse j-line orbifold)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold fundamental groups: Thurston and others. The Galois action on profinite SL_2(Z)/PSL_2(Z) through M_{1,1}: Nakamura, Ihara, Hain–Matsumoto (1990s–2000s).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses M_{1,1}, SL_2(Z) and 'groupes fondamentaux à singularités'. The circulated Longue Marche (1981) also has related material.

ideas.what: Requiring that the Γ-action on π̂_{0,3} fit into a morphism of extensions (σ) onto the PSL_2(Z)^-extension. This is read as a non-trivial condition on individual elements of Γ, to be made explicit, together with congruence conditions.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (2-cycle and 3-cycle/hexagon relations, linked to the 2- and 3-torsion of PSL_2(Z)); GT acting on profinite B_3 and PSL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1991); Lochak–Schneps (1997) on GT acting on braid groups and mapping class groups
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse states the program qualitatively. Explicit relations of this type are attributed to the Longue Marche manuscripts but were not published in that form.

ideas.what: The expectation of a whole 'kyrielle' of conditions of the same nature on Γ, to be extracted systematically. This aims at a combinatorial-geometric characterisation of the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in Out(π̂_{0,3}).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller program: Γ_Q versus GT, and the search for further relations (e.g. Hatcher–Thurston-type relations, higher levels of the Teichmüller tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak, Nakamura, Schneps and others

missed.claim: This is a dated manuscript record showing Grothendieck already obtaining conditions on Γ from compatibility with the 2/3-orbifold quotient (profinite PSL_2(Z)). On the following page this leads to the GT-type relations with γ = (ρ−1)/2, i.e. m = (λ−1)/2, well before Drinfeld. This is broadly known to specialists in outline (via the Longue Marche), but these specific equations are rarely quoted.
missed.quote: s'identifie au quotient de \hat\Pi_{0,3} par le sous-groupe invariant fermé engendré par l_1^2, l_\infty^3. Je commence à soupçonner qu'il y aura toute une kyrielle de conditions de même nature sur Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It helps document the priority and the conceptual origin of the GT relations: they come from orbifold/stack quotients of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, i.e. torsion in PSL_2(Z). Read that way, they appear as conditions extracted from stacky fundamental groups rather than from quasi-Hopf algebras.

missed.claim: The systematic extraction of the full 'kyrielle' of conditions on Γ from all such orbifold quotients (various weights on P^1 − {0,1,∞}) is left as a program on this page. Whether the resulting group differs from GT is related to the still-open question of whether Gal(Q̄/Q) → GT is surjective.
missed.quote: qu'il faudrait bien arriver à dégager de façon plus générale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Conditions coming from triangle-group quotients (weights other than 2 and 3) are a natural, not fully explored, source of candidate extra relations cutting GT down toward the image of Gal(Q̄/Q).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clear early instance of GT-type conditions arising from the PSL_2(Z)^-orbifold quotient. However, the Longue Marche is known to anticipate GT, and the orbifold viewpoint appears in the Esquisse. The novelty lies mainly in documentary detail and in the explicit triangle-group viewpoint as a source of conditions on Γ.
transcription_corrections: Margin: probably 'NB. E_{0,3} = le groupe M_{0,3}^! … voir §46'. The words after 'groupe' are uncertain; possibly 'noté' or 'donné'.

The struck phrase 'qui s'identifie à' is replaced by 'où le groupe M_{0,3}'. The parenthesis begins '(interprété comme "groupe fondamental" à singularités" de …)', with a struck initial letter before 'interprété'.
The base is written P^1 with a subscript that looks like Q (P^1_Q), consistent with Γ = Γ_Q.
'fermé' is an interlinear insertion above a struck 'engendré'. The intended reading is 'le sous-groupe invariant fermé engendré par l_1^2, l_∞^3'.
The lower-left group is written as Ĝ^+_{0,3} on this page; the previous-page transcription has \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} for what is likely the same symbol.
